$comment: PROTECTED FEATURE REGISTRY — LAYER 3 of the anti-regression system.
WHY: on 2026-08-21 production silently lost the 49-item dynamic throwables
because a build from a stale checkout replaced a current one. The first fix
was a hand-written test for that one feature. That does not scale: the next
feature to be silently erased would be the one nobody wrote a test for.
This file is the scaling mechanism. Every entry is a feature that EXISTS and
must keep existing. Two generic guards consume it:
tests/protectedFeatures.test.ts        (Club Arena) validates `source`
scripts/ci/check-ca-protected-features.mjs (World Hub) validates
`bundleMarkers` in the DEPLOYED
bundle
ADDING PROTECTION FOR A NEW FEATURE IS ONE ENTRY HERE. No new test file.
FIELD MEANINGS
files          paths that must exist (deletion = regression)
contains       { file: [strings] } every string must appear in that file
absent         { file: [strings] } none of these may appear (retired code
coming back is the signature of an old tree overwriting a
new one)
minCount       { file: { pattern, min } } occurrences must not fall below
min — a RATCHET that catches silent partial deletion
bundleMarkers  strings that must survive minification into the deployed
CSS/JS. Use load-bearing selectors, data-attributes and
custom properties; never a comment or a class that a
minifier may rename.
RULES
- Deliberately removing a feature means deleting its entry IN THE SAME
COMMIT, with the reason in the commit message. That makes removal a
visible, reviewable act instead of a silent disappearance.
- Never weaken an entry to make CI green. Fix the code.
- Ratchets go UP. Raise minCount when a feature grows; lowering one is a
deliberate, explained act.
